findings.title: Meet fallback crashes when no destination calendar is configured
findings.body: `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is undefined when `evt.destinationCalendar` is null or empty, but this condition reads `.integration` without optional chaining. A booking using Google Meet and no destination calendar therefore throws before calendar events are created, instead of applying the fallback or continuing normally.

findings.title: Calendar lookup cannot fall back when no external calendar ID is supplied
findings.body: When `externalCalendarId` is empty, this searches for a destination whose `externalId` equals that same empty value, so it returns `undefined` rather than selecting the event's destination calendar. The delete path repeats the same lookup at line 317. Updates/deletions without a reference calendar ID can consequently target no calendar (or the wrong default) instead of the configured destination.

findings.title: Collective host events use the first host's calendar address as organizer
findings.body: This code uses the first destination calendar's `externalId` for the organizer attendee on every calendar event, even though `createEvent` selects a different destination calendar for each credential. For collective bookings, events created on later hosts' calendars therefore identify the first host's calendar address as the organizer, leading to incorrect organizer identity and invitations.

findings.title: Recurring cancellation repeats deletes against the first calendar reference
findings.body: For each calendar reference, the recurring path loops over credentials and then uses `find` to select only the first calendar reference on each updated booking. With multiple calendar references, this repeats the same deletion for each outer reference and never deletes events identified by the other references. Collective recurring cancellations can leave events on hosts' calendars or issue duplicate deletion requests.
